where: The Old Light, floor 2 — The Late Laugh (a stage whose audience laughs a beat late)
mood: The Late Laugh — the same march with a lazy swing; every laugh arrives a beat after the joke.
_note: Classic oldlight-f2: 126, F major, the laughs start a beat late and spill over the barline. Opening shape: a lone stage-drum shuffle that the band falls in on, half a beat behind.
core_styles: 16-bit console RPG soundtrack from the mid-1990s
retro sampled-chip instruments with the warm echo of a 16-bit sound chip
stage pit band: muted trumpet lead, clarinet, tuba and banjo
the trombone laugh always lands one beat late, spilling over the barline
triangle echoing each phrase a beat behind
rimshot crash on the next downbeat, deliberately late
comic, a little sheepish, warm old theatre
strong singable melody, instantly hummable and pleasant on repeat

sections.name: Intro
sections.text: {a stage-drum shuffle and banjo vamp, the band tumbling in half a beat behind with a cheeky trumpet pickup}

sections.name: Main Theme
sections.text: {the march tune swung on muted trumpet over banjo and tuba; at each phrase end the slide-trombone laugh arrives a beat late and spills into the next bar}

sections.name: Main Theme Reprise
sections.text: {the tune again with clarinet answering a beat behind each phrase like an echo, triangle tings trailing the melody}

sections.name: Bridge
sections.text: {contrast: a soft-shoe shuffle in D minor, brushes and banjo, the clarinet sighing, a slide whistle late again, then a pickup back}

sections.name: Main Theme Return
sections.text: {the swung march returns full; the final late trombone laugh wraps over the barline straight back into the theme}
styles: seamless loop back to the start of the theme
